title: Microsoft AZ-900: Azure Fundamentals Study Guide
description: AZ-900 (Azure Fundamentals) is Microsoft's foundational cloud certification. The exam validates a broad understanding of cloud concepts and core Azure services, pricing, and governance—the most accessible entry point into the Microsoft Azure ecosystem.
audience: Beginners and career changers entering cloud, non-technical professionals (sales, finance, project management) who work with Azure, and IT pros who want an entry credential before tackling AZ-104 or other role-based Azure exams.
why_get_it: AZ-900 is the easiest way to get 'Azure certified' and prove cloud literacy in Microsoft environments. Azure is the dominant cloud in enterprise and government, so demonstrating you understand its services, pricing, and governance carries real weight—even in non-technical roles. For beginners it's a confidence-building first win and the foundation for the higher-value role-based certs (AZ-104, AZ-305, security and data tracks). Microsoft's free annual renewal model also means it costs little to maintain over time.
when_to_get_it: Get AZ-900 if you're new to cloud and want an approachable first Azure certification, or if your role touches Azure without being deeply technical. If you already have IT experience and a technical goal, you can often go straight to AZ-104—but AZ-900 is a low-cost, low-risk way to build a foundation and confidence first, and it's a common requirement in some training programs.
exam_format: Roughly 40–60 questions: multiple choice, multiple response, and other interactive formats. Passing score: 700 (on a scale of 100–1000).
recertification_note: Microsoft Fundamentals certifications like AZ-900 do not expire—they have no renewal requirement. (Role-based certs such as AZ-104 renew annually for free via a Microsoft Learn assessment.)
salary_note: AZ-900 is a foundational credential, not a salary driver on its own—it typically adds a few thousand dollars to an existing IT salary and helps open the door to entry cloud roles ($50K–$70K). Its real value is as a stepping stone: pairing it with AZ-104 and hands-on Azure experience moves you toward the $75K–$110K administrator range and beyond.

items: The benefits and considerations of cloud computing
Infrastructure-, platform-, and software-as-a-service (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS)
Public, private, and hybrid cloud models
Capital vs operational expenditure and the consumption model
High availability, scalability, elasticity, and disaster recovery
Core architectural components: Regions, Availability Zones, resource groups
Compute services: virtual machines, App Service, containers, functions
Identity: Microsoft Entra ID and authentication concepts
Cost management: pricing calculator, TCO, and cost controls
Governance: tags, policies, resource locks, and Azure Policy
Tools for managing and deploying resources (portal, CLI, ARM/Bicep)
Monitoring tools: Azure Monitor, Service Health, and advisories

study_steps.title: Read the official AZ-900 study guide
study_steps.description: Microsoft publishes a free AZ-900 study guide listing every skill measured and the latest exam updates. Start here so you study exactly what's tested—the objectives change periodically.

study_steps.title: Work through the free Microsoft Learn path
study_steps.description: Microsoft Learn has a free, structured AZ-900 learning path that covers 100% of the objectives with hands-on exercises. It's the single best free resource and uses the exact terminology the exam uses.

study_steps.title: Add a paid video course for structure
study_steps.description: A paid course (Scott Duffy's on Udemy is the most popular) adds a clear narrative and demos on top of Microsoft Learn. Helpful if you prefer video and want everything in one place. See the paid resources section.

study_steps.title: Create a free Azure account and explore
study_steps.description: Sign up for a free Azure account and click through the portal: create a resource group, deploy a VM, open Cost Management. A little hands-on time makes the services and governance topics concrete.

study_steps.title: Use the official free practice assessment
study_steps.description: Microsoft provides a free official AZ-900 practice assessment. It mirrors the real question style closely—use it to find weak areas before booking.

study_steps.title: Take additional practice exams
study_steps.description: Work through more full-length AZ-900 practice tests. Aim to score consistently above 85% before booking. Review every miss until the concept is clear.

study_steps.title: Schedule and sit the exam
study_steps.description: Register through Pearson VUE (test center or online proctored). The exam is short—about 45 minutes. Check for Microsoft's free voucher promotions (Learn challenges) before paying full price.

faq.question: Is AZ-900 worth it?
faq.answer: For beginners and non-technical roles, yes. It's the easiest way to get Azure-certified and prove cloud literacy, and it's a foundation for the higher-value role-based certs. Experienced IT pros with a technical goal sometimes skip straight to AZ-104.

faq.question: How hard is the AZ-900 exam?
faq.answer: It's the easiest Azure exam—foundational and broad. Most candidates pass with a couple of weeks of study using the free Microsoft Learn path plus practice questions. No hands-on technical depth is required.

faq.question: Does AZ-900 expire?
faq.answer: No. Microsoft Fundamentals certifications, including AZ-900, do not expire and have no renewal requirement. (Role-based certs like AZ-104 renew annually for free.)

faq.question: Do I need experience before AZ-900?
faq.answer: No. There are no prerequisites, and it's designed for beginners and non-technical professionals. A free Azure account for hands-on clicking is the only 'experience' you need.

faq.question: AZ-900 or AZ-104 — which should I take?
faq.answer: AZ-900 is foundational and non-technical; AZ-104 is the role-based administrator cert and far more in-demand for jobs. If you have IT experience, you can often skip to AZ-104. If you're new, AZ-900 builds a foundation first.

faq.question: How long does it take to study for AZ-900?
faq.answer: Most candidates spend 1 to 3 weeks part-time. The free Microsoft Learn path plus the official practice assessment is enough for many people. Those with IT backgrounds may be ready in a few days.

faq.question: What comes after AZ-900?
faq.answer: The role-based certs: AZ-104 (Administrator) is the usual next step, with AZ-305 (Architect), AZ-500 (Security), and others beyond. SC-900 and AI-900 are sibling fundamentals if you want broader Microsoft coverage.

related_certs.title: Microsoft AZ-104
related_certs.reason: The role-based administrator cert and the usual next step after AZ-900. Where AZ-900 proves literacy, AZ-104 proves you can manage Azure day to day.

related_certs.title: Microsoft SC-900
related_certs.reason: The security, compliance, and identity fundamentals cert. A natural sibling to AZ-900 for building broad Microsoft cloud knowledge.

related_certs.title: AWS Cloud Practitioner
related_certs.reason: The AWS equivalent foundational cloud cert. Many beginners get both to demonstrate cross-cloud literacy.
